claims.statement: deepagents-code (dcode) is a prebuilt terminal coding agent that packages the deepagents SDK harness together with a terminal experience, persistence, tools, skills, and optional sandboxed execution, as a reference implementation.

dcode has two runtime halves that run in separate processes: a terminal client that owns presentation and input (interactive or headless output plus approvals), and an agent server that owns the agent runtime and connects the model, tools, memory, skills, and backend.

Approval mode is a validated per-thread live record whose key is a SHA-256 digest of the thread ID; invalid, unavailable, or unreadable store records fail closed to Manual, while the interactive cycle conditionally offers Auto and YOLO.

Before first interactive enable, Auto requires explicit Enter confirmation and YOLO requires explicit acknowledgement; cancellation does not persist their local records or activate the requested mode, and YOLO's Manual choice changes to Manual instead.

dcode constrains Textual to versions 8.2.8 through before 9 because UI patches and custom rendering depend on upstream behavior and private wrapping/compositor offset contracts; message pointer hit testing specifically relies on the private `offset` style metadata.

`DeepAgentsApp` composes the startup tip, goal-status panel, chat input, and docked status bar; after first paint it constructs the Textual adapter with callbacks for rendering, approvals, status, accounting, skills, and Auto-mode events before starting background initialization.

The two-line status bar keeps hook and agent messages in separate slots so hooks override only while nonempty, uses plain `Content` for hook-configured text, and shares one spinner between connection and busy indications that is stopped on unmount.

The app surfaces alternate-screen startup advisories after refresh, including unavailable interpreter configuration, sandbox-suppressed interpreter, disabled tracing, and Auto restoration failure; these notifications are best-effort UI feedback while logged diagnostics remain durable.

Modal continuations reached from the Textual message pump are detached because awaiting them inline would prevent Enter/Esc dispatch; admission allows one global continuation, reports conflicts, tracks task failure, and resumes queued-message draining after completion.

After an approval selection succeeds, dcode records Manual or Auto as a startup preference but never YOLO; if that preference write fails, the active session mode remains in effect and the app warns the user.

dcode pins its Deep Agents SDK dependency exactly to `deepagents==0.7.28`; package guidance requires bumping that pin with SDK-dependent features and describes CI validation against an outdated release pin.
The distribution publishes both `dcode` and `deepagents-code` console scripts to the same `cli_main` entrypoint, and `--version` can report installed optional dependencies.

Slash commands are defined once with a queue-bypass tier; derived tier sets include aliases, and `/install`, `/reload`, and `/update` remain startup-failure recovery escape hatches despite normally being queue-bound.
The optional dependency surface provides individual provider extras and an `all-providers` composite, plus sandbox extras and an `all-sandboxes` composite.

dcode's retry middleware wraps the model node rather than a whole turn, preserving completed tool calls during transient model retries; it tracks streamed output so retry rendering can mark potentially partial output as incomplete.

The app checks prompt-cache expiry and final-window notifications once per second after post-paint initialization; final-window warnings are deduplicated per thread and expiry, withheld during reconciliation, and hook notification failures do not block the UI.

A reconciled expired prompt cache displays an expiry banner independently of handoff preferences; a cache window already expired when a resumed thread loads is marked seen to avoid an immediate idle interruption.

When the cache-expiry warning mode is enabled, dcode offers a handoff only when idle and otherwise gates an expired interactive submission through a detached modal; cancellation or handoff preserves the draft, while inability to admit the modal also restores it rather than dispatching silently.

`ServerConfig` is the shared client-to-server configuration schema: the launcher writes its serialized `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SERVER_*` mapping and the server reconstructs it with `from_env`; relative paths are normalized before serialization because the subprocess has a different working directory.

The server, not the client, authorizes project-scoped workspace policy: it rejects claimed project fields, verifies the client-claimable session policy fingerprint, resolves policy for the canonical target directory, and persists the server-authoritative workspace payload with the thread binding.

Changing workspace directories fails closed for project execution policy: dcode drops launch-project MCP configuration, sandbox setup, and extension paths, then re-reads extension trust for the target project instead of applying one checkout's policy to another.

Slash-command completion uses registry-derived command entries, scores canonical names, aliases, hidden keywords, descriptions, and fuzzy matches, and inserts a command's machine name rather than its displayed label so namespaced skills remain addressable.
The completion system reserves `@@` for durable thread references and inserts `@@(thread:<id>)`; thread suggestions search session metadata and sanitize/fall back their visible labels.

Sandbox provider discovery merges built-ins, entry points, and user configuration with precedence config over entry point over built-in; metadata supplies capability and install information used by lifecycle and preflight checks.

`create_sandbox` validates snapshot capability and disallows snapshots with an existing sandbox ID, runs optional setup inside the acquired backend, and deletes only sandboxes it created; cleanup runs after setup or caller failures and cleanup errors do not mask the primary failure.

The retry middleware emits correlated model-attempt lifecycle events and retry events, reads provider retry budget from each request model, and bounds total interactive retry delay to 60 seconds; malformed lifecycle payloads are ignored rather than trusted.
